title: GTA 5's Michael Actor Defends GTA 6 Against Critics
description: Ned Luke, the actor behind GTA 5's Michael, sharply defends GTA 6 after doubters claimed Rockstar's upcoming open-world game looks too similar to its predecessor.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 5 Star Ned Luke Defends GTA 6 After Visual Doubts

As the gaming community eagerly awaits the arrival of Rockstar Games' next monumental release, discussions and debates surrounding the title are inevitable. Recently, a segment of observers and players voiced a rather critical viewpoint, suggesting that Grand Theft Auto 6 looks too similar to Grand Theft Auto 5. However, this comparison did not sit well with everyone, notably prompting a sharp and direct response from one of the most iconic faces of the previous installment.

### "Out of Their Minds"

According to IGN Games, Ned Luke—the actor who brought Michael De Santa to life in Grand Theft Auto 5 through performance capture and voice acting—fired back at the doubters. Luke bluntly stated that people who think GTA 6 looks too much like GTA 5 are "out of their minds." His candid remark quickly circulated across gaming forums and social media platforms, reigniting discussions about visual evolution and franchise consistency.

Maintaining a distinct artistic direction while pushing technological boundaries is a challenging task for any premier developer. Rockstar Games has a well-documented history of evolving its proprietary engine and systems between releases, as seen in the massive leaps from GTA 4 to GTA 5, and subsequently to Red Dead Redemption 2. While familiar urban settings or stylistic choices might evoke a sense of nostalgia or perceived repetition at first glance, the underlying technical complexity, physics, and world density typically undergo massive upgrades.

### Expectations vs. Reality

It is common for early promotional materials or trailers of highly anticipated games to spark intense scrutiny and debate regarding graphics. Luke's defense highlights the gap between superficial first impressions and the extensive engineering effort required to build a modern, next-generation open-world masterpiece. As development continues, fans will undoubtedly look forward to further insights from the creators and actors who know the inner workings of Rockstar's ambitious pipeline best.

### Editor's Take

Ned Luke's passionate defense of Grand Theft Auto 6 reminds us why the community remains so deeply connected to the franchise. Judging a massive open-world sequel based solely on superficial visual comparisons overlooks the profound technical and systemic innovations happening beneath the surface.
